risks.note: All manufacturing is carried out at one facility at Petlad, Gujarat, and the Company operates in a single business segment — spinning of technical textile yarn. Any disruption, slowdown or shutdown at Petlad, or adverse developments in that one segment, hits the entire business with no alternative site or offsetting vertical.

Top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 customers contributed 19.75% / 39.77% / 51.57% / 67.40% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 (25.53% / 47.85% / 57.91% / 72.11% in Fiscal 2024). Loss of one large customer, a decline in its financial health or reduced demand would materially affect revenue and cash flow. China alone accounted for 19.75% of Fiscal 2025 revenue, matching the top-1 customer figure.

There are no long-term agreements for supply of raw materials, and the majority is sourced from the top 10 suppliers (70.31% of purchases in Fiscal 2025). Para-aramid, viscose and acrylic fibres come from a limited number of customer-approved suppliers, so substitution is slow and disruption or price escalation passes into production schedules, volumes and margins.
risks.risk: Raw material dependence without long-term supply agreements

risks.note: The business is heavily dependent on para-aramid based spun yarn and 100% polypropylene spun yarn, disclosed at 23.87% and 22.64% of revenue from operations respectively in Fiscal 2025 (32.10% and 21.27% in Fiscal 2024). business_ops.supply_chain_integration: BACKWARD INTEGRATION - proprietary 'Fabric-to-Fibre' recycling. The Company imports end-of-life para-aramid fabrics (e.g. expired bulletproof vests) and processes them through a dedicated regenerating machine for high-strength fibres, converting them into secondary raw material used in brake pads, clutch facings, filtration media and protective textiles. Para Aramid Fabric Waste purchases were Rs 1,409.18 / 1,429.71 / 2,509.24 lakhs against total purchases of Rs 6,568.07 / 7,295.41 / 7,227.68 lakhs in FY26 / FY25 / FY24, being 21.46% / 19.60% / 34.72% of total purchase (the RHP's own computed line). The RHP states this reduces dependence on imported virgin fibres and lowers raw material costs. orders_not_placed.note: AFFIRMATIVE, EXPLICIT, AND UNAMBIGUOUS. The RHP states in Note 1 to the capex table: 'We have considered the above quotations for the budgetary estimate purpose and have not placed orders for them. No orders have been placed with any of the aforementioned vendors.' Every column heading in the table reads 'Date of Quotation' and 'Validity of Quotation' - there is no purchase-order column, no PO number anywhere, and no advance paid. There is therefore NO ambiguous quotation-or-PO row in this filing. THE PERCENTAGE IS DERIVED, NOT STATED: the RHP prints no un-ordered percentage. 100.0 is obtained by direct summation of the capex table - all 21 line items across 5 suppliers, totalling the document-stated 2,550.83 lakhs (Total A 459.89 + Total B 2,090.94), carry quotations only, so 2,550.83 / 2,550.83 = 100.0%. UNREPLACED BOILERPLATE NOTED: two sentences after 'No orders have been placed with any of the aforementioned vendors', the same Note 1 says the Promoters, Directors, KMP and Group Companies have no interest in 'the entity from whom we have placed or may place purchase orders'. The 'have placed' limb is generic template phrasing that sits against the explicit no-orders statement in the immediately preceding sentence; weighing by evidence, the no-orders statement governs - it is specific, repeated twice in one paragraph, and matched by a table with no purchase-order column, no PO number and no advance anywhere. THE FINDING - QUOTATION VALIDITY VERSUS THE DEPLOYMENT SCHEDULE: all 20 quotations are dated July 17, 2026, five weeks before the August 24, 2026 RHP date. The deployment schedule commits the entire 2,550.83 lakhs to Financial Year 2027, i.e. through March 31, 2027. NOT ONE quotation remains valid to the end of that window. The LMW Limited block - Blow Room, Carding (main and accessories), Draw Frame LDB3, Auto leveller Draw Frame LDF3S, Speed Frame LF4280A and Ring Frame LRJ9SX/SXL, together 988.22 lakhs, which is 38.74% of the capex by direct summation of those seven rows - is valid only to August 31, 2026, SEVEN DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF THIS RED HERRING PROSPECTUS and roughly seven months before the end of the stated deployment window; it contains the single largest line item in the table (Ring Frame, 607.11 lakhs). The remaining 1,562.61 lakhs (61.26%, derived as the document-stated total 2,550.83 less the LMW block 988.22; the four other vendors' rows sum to 1,562.62 - Parmeshwar Construction 459.89, Vandewiele Savio India 1,019.87, SMEW Textile Machinery 28.32, Adishwar Electricals 54.54) is valid to January 13, 2027, still two months and eighteen days short of the March 31, 2027 end of the deployment window. The RHP itself concedes the exposure: 'The actual cost of procurement and actual supplier/dealer may vary.' ARITHMETIC NOTE: the seven LMW rows sum to 988.22 and the fifteen equipment rows sum to 2,090.95 against the document-stated Total (B) of 2,090.94, and all 21 rows sum to 2,550.84 against the document-stated Total (A + B) of 2,550.83 - a one-paisa rounding difference in the filing, not an extraction error; the document-stated subtotals are the ones carried into the breakdown above and used as denominators. overview.business_model: The Company operates on a business-to-business model, supplying specialised yarns and fabrics directly to industrial manufacturers, processors and institutional buyers rather than to retail consumers. It manufactures either as part of its own product range or on a job-work basis depending on client requirements, with products customised to client technical specifications. Manufacturing runs on five distinct processing lines using three yarn technologies installed at its facility: Ring Spun (2 Ne to 50 Ne, single or up to six-ply), DREF friction-spun (0.4 Ne to 2.5 Ne, mainly filter cartridges) and Open-End spinning (2 Ne to 4 Ne, gas filter bags and carpet backing). The product range includes para-aramid, meta-aramid, modacrylic-blended, peroxidised PAN, antistatic polypropylene, FR Viscose blends and DREF-spun yarns with glass filament cores or aramid sheaths. End-markets stated are filtration and pollution control, construction and infrastructure (geotextiles, ropes, webbings), automotive friction materials and thermal insulation, packaging (antistatic FIBC), safety and protective equipment, and home furnishing. The RHP states the Company engaged with 109, 130 and 128 customers and 49, 58 and 55 suppliers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, and describes the model as emphasising recurring supply to industrial clients.

verdict_pointers: Capital history is dominated by one event: a bonus issue in the ratio of 8:1 allotted on September 15, 2025 (1,40,00,000 shares), which took paid-up capital from 17,50,000 shares to 1,57,50,000 shares. Every per-share figure in the RHP divides by the post-bonus count. The bonus was allotted 11 months and 9 days before the RHP date of August 24, 2026 (this interval is DERIVED arithmetic by this extraction from the two printed dates, not a statement in the RHP). The RHP's own Basis for Issue Price disclosure states there was no primary issuance during the 18 months preceding the RHP that was equal to or more than 5% of fully diluted capital, expressly EXCLUDING bonus shares from that test.

Face value was sub-divided from Rs 1,000 per share to Rs 10 per share on June 14, 2024 (100:1 split), affecting both authorised and paid-up capital. Any pre-June-2024 share count in the RHP is on the Rs 1,000 face value.

The RHP states affirmatively at Note (B) of the Basis for Issue Price and again in the Issue chapter that 'The proposed Issue is fresh issue and there is no Offer for Sale (OFS) by any shareholders.' This is an affirmative nil, not an absence.

DERIVED BY THIS EXTRACTION (not printed in the RHP): comparing the RHP's 1%-shareholder table 'as on the date of the Red Herring Prospectus' against its table 'as on date ten days prior to the date of the Red Herring Prospectus', 12,50,000 equity shares (7.94% of pre-issue paid-up capital) changed hands in that ten-day window. The RHP prints no narrative explanation of these transfers and does not identify which transferor sold to which transferee. Its Secondary Transactions disclosure covers only transactions to which a Promoter, Promoter Group member or a shareholder with the right to nominate directors is a party; none of the four transferors above is named among the five Promoter & Promoter Group shareholders (Prahash Fin-Stock Private Limited, Abhishek Rajendrakumar Agarwal, Siddharth Prakash Patel, Shree Bajrangbali Intermediate & Dyechem Private Limited, R.K. Agarwal Trading Company Private Limited) nor in the Promoter Group lists in the promoters chapter, so this movement falls outside that disclosure. The RHP addresses the point affirmatively at Capital Structure Note 16: 'There were no shares purchased/sold by the Promoter(s) and Promoter Group, directors of our Company and their relatives during last six months from the date of filing of this Red Herring Prospectus' - which, if the transferors are neither promoters, promoter group, directors nor relatives of directors, is consistent with the movement computed above. Note 17 adds that the members of the Promoters' Group, the directors and the relatives of the directors have not financed the purchase by any other person of securities of the Company, other than in the normal course of the business of the financing entity, during the six months immediately preceding the RHP date. Who acquired the 12,50,000 shares from whom, and on what terms, is an OPEN QUESTION the RHP does not address - not an assertion of any breach.

litigation_summary.materiality_threshold_basis: Materiality Policy adopted by Board resolution dated July 28, 2026 (as stated in the chapter preamble). For 'other pending litigation/arbitration' a matter is material if the aggregate monetary claim/dispute/liability exceeds the lowest of: (i) 2% of revenue from operations = Rs 234.74 lakhs; (ii) 2% of net worth = Rs 103.79 lakhs; (iii) 5% of the average of the absolute value of profit or loss after tax for the last three financial years = Rs 52.67 lakhs. Rs 52.67 lakhs, being the lowest, is the stated Threshold. A matter is also material if its outcome could have a material adverse effect irrespective of amount or quantifiability, or if the decision is likely to affect similar proceedings such that the cumulative amount exceeds the Threshold. Criminal proceedings, statutory/regulatory actions and direct/indirect tax claims are disclosed irrespective of the Threshold, being carved out of the Threshold test as items (i) to (iii) of the disclosure scope.
litigation_summary.matters_below_threshold: Every matter disclosed against the Company (Rs 0.77 lakhs) and against the Promoters (Rs 2.72 lakhs) is below the Rs 52.67 lakhs Threshold. They are disclosed because they are tax proceedings, which fall outside the Threshold test. The Group Companies aggregate of Rs 184.54 lakhs exceeds the Threshold; the chapter carries a footnote that the Group Companies section 'only contains litigations involving amounts exceeding the materiality threshold'.

concerns_observed: The entire profitability step-up is one year old and the RHP gives no bridge for it: EBITDA margin 14.69% -> 15.64% -> 26.47% and PAT ₹704.94 -> 850.92 -> 1,604.23 lakhs on revenue that grew only 2.93% in FY26 (DERIVED from 11,403.40 -> 11,737.14). Other income fell 93.58% to ₹6.03 lakhs, so the gain is not there either; the RHP prints the margins and explains none of the movement.

A large part of the capital structure is related-party money on demand: unsecured loans of ₹1,842.80 lakhs at 31-Mar-2026 are stated by RF39 to be wholly from related parties, of which ₹1,087.80 lakhs is repayable on demand at 10-12% with no amortisation schedule - 38.45% of total debt (DERIVED, 1,842.80 / 4,792.45). Related-party interest expense of ₹194.79 lakhs is 41.62% of the ₹468.04 lakh finance-cost line (DERIVED). Both operating premises are leased from promoter-connected parties: the Petlad factory from Shyam Prakash Spinning Mills, a group company in which promoter Siddharth Prakash Patel holds 6.11%, and the registered office from Pitex Corporation, 25% held by a promoter's wife. Annexure XXXIV carries 390 related-party rows.

Concentration runs through customers, products, geography and site at once: top-1 customer 21.80% and top-5 51.83% of FY26 revenue, against which RF13 states the Company has no long-term purchase commitments with most customers and that orders are placed on immediate requirements; China alone is 21.80% of revenue; para-aramid and 100% polypropylene yarns are 50.61% of revenue (DERIVED, 27.66% + 22.95%); all manufacturing sits at one leased facility at Petlad; and the RHP states it has no long-term or exclusive supply agreements with any supplier.

The consented capacity and the announced expansion do not line up, and the RHP does not reconcile them: the GPCB Consent-to-Establish amendment (CTE-89559, 27-Oct-2025) covers an additional 92 MT per month, i.e. 1,104 MTPA on a straight 12-month basis (DERIVED), against the 1,250 MTPA expansion stated in both the Objects and Business chapters. A separate MGVCL application to raise sanctioned load from 1,805 KVA to 3,000 KVA, made 30-Aug-2025, has been pending about 12 months on the same facility the Objects fund; the RHP does not state whether commissioning depends on it.

Receivables have aged sharply: ₹209.80 lakhs was outstanding beyond one year at 31-Mar-2026, 9.79% of the ₹2,143.77 lakh gross book, against ₹2.97 lakhs a year earlier and ₹11.13 lakhs two years earlier. The expansion dilutes utilisation on its own arithmetic: adding 1,250 MTPA to 4,775 MTPA takes implied utilisation to 76.49% (DERIVED by this extraction from the RHP's own 96.51% on the expanding line), while the existing 100% polypropylene line has run at 63.95% / 63.75% / 66.38% for three years on unchanged 1,025 MTPA of dedicated, non-interchangeable machinery.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: BACKWARD INTEGRATION - proprietary 'Fabric-to-Fibre' recycling. The Company imports end-of-life para-aramid fabrics (e.g. expired bulletproof vests) and processes them through a dedicated regenerating machine for high-strength fibres, converting them into secondary raw material used in brake pads, clutch facings, filtration media and protective textiles. Para Aramid Fabric Waste purchases were Rs 1,409.18 / 1,429.71 / 2,509.24 lakhs against total purchases of Rs 6,568.07 / 7,295.41 / 7,227.68 lakhs in FY26 / FY25 / FY24, being 21.46% / 19.60% / 34.72% of total purchase (the RHP's own computed line). The RHP states this reduces dependence on imported virgin fibres and lowers raw material costs. CAPTIVE ENERGY INTEGRATION - a 380 KW rooftop solar system at the Petlad unit (MGVCL connection released January 19, 2022) plus a ground-mounted solar plant on leased land at Kankanpur described as 4 MW (Our Business) / 5 MW DC and 4 MW AC (History chapter), commissioned per GETCO certificate of February 07, 2025 and GEDA certificate of April 30, 2025, which the RHP states 'has substituted a significant portion of our electricity requirements from Financial Year 2025-26 onwards'. FORWARD INTEGRATION (PROPOSED, NOT YET REVENUE-GENERATING) - the Company proposes to move downstream from modacrylic-based yarn into the manufacture and sale of modacrylic-based fabrics; this is being trialled through job work with third-party weaving units and third-party process houses, i.e. asset-light and NOT in-house weaving, with captive consumption of its own modacrylic yarn. NOT INTEGRATED / EXPOSED - the Company has no long-term or exclusive supply agreements with any supplier and no long-term purchase commitments with most customers; purchases are made on purchase orders that may be discontinued, modified or cancelled without significant prior notice. A large proportion of specialty fibres (para-aramid, meta-aramid, modacrylic, FR viscose) is imported: imports were 36.29% / 36.92% / 41.18% of total purchase in FY26 / FY25 / FY24 versus domestic 63.71% / 63.08% / 58.82%. Raw material and traded goods purchases were 68.51% / 70.23% / 72.20% of total expenses. Sourcing locations named: Gujarat, Maharashtra, China, USA, Thailand and Brazil. The Company avails duty-free imports under the Advance Authorisation Scheme and imports capital goods under the EPCG Scheme, both carrying export obligations. The Company holds no collaboration or performance-guarantee/marketing-assistance arrangement with any company, and has no holding company, subsidiary or joint venture. Distribution is direct B2B to industrial manufacturers, processors and institutional buyers, supported by participation in Messe Frankfurt exhibitions in Germany, Mumbai and Russia; there is no distributor or dealer network disclosed. Defect and rejection rates were 0.13% / 0.40% / 0.03% of revenue from operations in FY26 / FY25 / FY24. Average relationship length: approximately 6 years with major customers and approximately 5.5 years with major suppliers.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- All manufacturing is carried out at one facility at Petlad, Gujarat, and the Company operates in a single business segment — spinning of technical textile yarn. Any disruption, slowdown or shutdown at Petlad, or adverse developments in that one segment, hits the entire business with no alternative site or offsetting vertical.
- Top 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 customers contributed 19.75% / 39.77% / 51.57% / 67.40% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 (25.53% / 47.85% / 57.91% / 72.11% in Fiscal 2024). Loss of one large customer, a decline in its financial health or reduced demand would materially affect revenue and cash flow. China alone accounted for 19.75% of Fiscal 2025 revenue, matching the top-1 customer figure.
- There are no long-term agreements for supply of raw materials, and the majority is sourced from the top 10 suppliers (70.31% of purchases in Fiscal 2025). Para-aramid, viscose and acrylic fibres come from a limited number of customer-approved suppliers, so substitution is slow and disruption or price escalation passes into production schedules, volumes and margins.
- The business is heavily dependent on para-aramid based spun yarn and 100% polypropylene spun yarn, disclosed at 23.87% and 22.64% of revenue from operations respectively in Fiscal 2025 (32.10% and 21.27% in Fiscal 2024). Any fall in demand, inability to produce, or adverse price movement in these two yarns disproportionately affects results.
- The registered office, the Petlad manufacturing unit, the rooftop solar facility and the 4 MW ground-mounted solar project are all on leased property, and the Issue proceeds will install machinery on a leased factory. Early termination, non-renewal, or renewal on worse terms would jeopardise both operations and the return on Issue-funded capex.
- Exports were 38.05% of Fiscal 2025 revenue from operations and the Company carries an obligation to export against import of ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025 (₹ 343.53 lakhs in Fiscal 2024). Failure to meet export obligations, or adverse changes in foreign trade policy or tariffs, would trigger duty liabilities and hurt cash flows.
- Debt-equity ratio rose to 1.60x in Fiscal 2025 from 1.27x, long-term borrowings grew 120.11% to ₹ 3,090.25 lakhs and short-term borrowings included director loans of ₹ 1,289.30 lakhs; short loans received from related parties were ₹ 1,778.63 lakhs in Fiscal 2025. The Company has also experienced negative cash flows in the recent past. ₹ 2,500.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked to repay borrowings, so post-Issue re-leveraging is the item to watch.
- The proposed expansion depends on purchasing and installing new equipment and machinery for ₹ 2,495.75 lakhs against quotations, not firm orders, deployed across Fiscals 2026 and 2027. If investment in manufacturing technology falls short, or the added capacity is not absorbed at the assumed demand (an estimated 120 MT against present 55 MT capability), competitiveness and returns suffer.

- **Outstanding obligation to export against import under duty exemption schemes stood at ₹ 535.82 lakhs as at March 31, 2025, up from ₹ 343.53 lakhs a year earlier; non-compliance would trigger duty liabilities.**
